definition: Objective Vision (Object Oriented Visionary) is a project mainly aimed at real-time computer vision and simulation vision of living creatures.
details: it has three sections containing an open-source library of programming functions for using inside the projects, Virtual laboratory for scholars to check the application of functions directly and by command-line code for external and instant access, and the research section consists of paperwork and libraries to expand the scientific prove of works.

explainer.lead: Objective Vision is a project aimed at real-time computer vision and simulation vision of living creatures. It is organised into three sections: an open-source library, a virtual laboratory, and research material.

tiers.eli5: It is a toolkit plus a lab and a research area, all aimed at helping computers see and simulate living things in real time.
tiers.practitioner: Developers use the open-source library's functions inside their own projects and check them in the virtual laboratory or via command-line code for instant access. A pitfall is that the project spans library, lab and research, so verifying results requires moving between all three.
tiers.paperLevel: A project for real-time computer vision and simulation vision of living creatures, comprising an open-source function library, a virtual laboratory for scholars to check function application directly and via command-line code, and a research section of paperwork and libraries to expand scientific proof of works.

explainer.example: A scholar opens the virtual laboratory, applies a library function to a sample, and checks the result directly.
